Assortative planted-partition stochastic block model

pp_block_state.Rd

Native C++ implementation of the microcanonical Bayesian planted-partition stochastic block model (Zhang and Peixoto 2020), matching graph-tool's PPBlockState. Constrains community structure to assortative (or disassortative) block patterns parameterized only by within-community edges \(E_{\mathrm{in}}\) and between-community edges \(E_{\mathrm{out}}\), and provides declarative model comparison against the general flat and nested SBMs.

Usage

pp_block_state(graph, blocks = NULL, uniform = FALSE,
  degree_corrected = TRUE, degree_prior = c("distributed", "uniform"))
pp_description_length(state, degree_prior = NULL)
pp_assortativity(state)
minimize_pp_blockmodel_dl(graph, uniform = FALSE, degree_corrected = TRUE,
  degree_prior = c("distributed", "uniform"), B_min = 1L, B_max = Inf,
  refine = TRUE, epsilon = 1e-3)
compare_assortative_models(graph,
  models = c("pp", "pp_uniform", "sbm_flat", "sbm_nested"),
  degree_corrected = TRUE, degree_prior = c("distributed", "uniform"),
  method = c("map", "posterior"),
  evidence_method = c("variational", "importance"),
  nruns = 1L, nsamples = 200L, thin = 5L, burnin = NULL, mle = TRUE,
  B_min = 1L, B_max = Inf, refine = TRUE)

Arguments

graph

A graph created by graph_create.

blocks

Optional integer vector of 1-based group memberships of length graph_num_vertices(graph). Defaults to a single group.

uniform

If FALSE (the default), use the non-uniform planted-partition model where each community \(r\) has its own internal edge count \(e_{rr}\); if TRUE, constrain all communities to share a uniform internal rate.

degree_corrected

Whether to fit the degree-corrected (TRUE) or non-degree-corrected (FALSE) planted-partition model.

degree_prior

Degree sequence hyperprior ("distributed" or "uniform").

state

A rgraphtool_pp_block_state created by pp_block_state() or minimize_pp_blockmodel_dl().

B_min, B_max

Minimum and maximum number of occupied groups.

refine

Whether to run greedy refinement sweeps after merge-split minimization.

epsilon

Stopping tolerance in nats for greedy refinement.

models

Character vector naming a subset of "pp", "pp_uniform", "sbm_flat", and "sbm_nested" to compare.

method

Compare models by "map" minimum description length or full Bayesian "posterior" marginal evidence.

evidence_method

Evidence estimator forwarded to model_evidence when method = "posterior".

nruns

Number of independent minimization restarts per model.

nsamples, thin, burnin, mle

Posterior sampling and entropy estimation controls forwarded to model_evidence.

Details

Unlike the general SBM, which estimates an arbitrary \(B \times B\) block affinity matrix, the planted-partition model restricts off-diagonal interactions to a single global rate while modeling internal edges either per-community (uniform = FALSE) or uniformly (uniform = TRUE). This gives \(O(B)\) state memory and zero-allocation incremental moves while remaining free of modularity's resolution limit and overfitting on random graphs.

Planted-partition states work directly with block_membership, block_sizes, mcmc_sweep, mcmc_equilibrate, mcmc_anneal, sample_posterior, and model_evidence.

Value

pp_block_state() and minimize_pp_blockmodel_dl() return a rgraphtool_pp_block_state list with blocks, graph, uniform, degree_corrected, degree_prior, B, and optional fit.

pp_description_length() returns the exact microcanonical description length in nats.

pp_assortativity() returns a list with E_in, E_out, E_total, fraction_in, B, effective group count Be, and per-group internal edge counts err.

compare_assortative_models() returns a rgraphtool_assortative_model_comparison list with ranked summary, best_model, best_state, states, optional evidences, and log_bayes_factors.

References

Zhang, L. and Peixoto, T. P. (2020). Statistical inference of assortative community structures. Physical Review Research 2, 043271. doi:10.1103/PhysRevResearch.2.043271

See also

minimize_blockmodel_dl, minimize_nested_blockmodel_dl, mcmc_sweep, model_evidence, demo("assortative_sbm")

Examples

g <- graph_create(12, directed = FALSE)
graph_add_edges(g, rbind(t(combn(1:6, 2)), t(combn(7:12, 2)), c(1, 7)))
set.seed(1)
st <- minimize_pp_blockmodel_dl(g)
st
#> <planted-partition block state: degree-corrected, non-uniform assortativity, B = 2 (Be = 2.00), E_in/E = 96.8%, DL = 55.1833 nats>
pp_assortativity(st)
#> $E_in
#> [1] 30
#> 
#> $E_out
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $E_total
#> [1] 31
#> 
#> $fraction_in
#> [1] 0.9677419
#> 
#> $B
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $Be
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $err
#> [1] 15 15
#>
